subject: Quantumpay service disruption: closure brief & remediation commitments
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jul 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quantumpay service disruption: closure brief & remediation commitments

Samir —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the investigation. Attached is a concise closure brief that summarizes the root cause, the event timeline, immediate mitigations we performed, and the committed short- and medium-term actions. High level: 

- Root cause: an autoscaling regression in our model routing layer that caused stale capacity decisions when an internal runtime metric exceeded a threshold. This produced sustained request queueing for ~22 minutes and increased token latency for a subset of your production traffic.
- Impact window: 2029-07-26T22:49:00Z to 2029-07-26T23:11:00Z (22 minutes).
- Customer-facing severity: elevated error rates and latency spikes for the Quantumpay production tenant during the window; no data exfiltration or model state corruption.

What we are delivering in this packet:
1) Summarized RCA (high-level) — included in this email body and the PDF appendix.
2) Annotated event timeline (CSV) — precise timestamps and owner notes for each mitigation step.
3) Action register — owners, ETA, verification steps (spreadsheet).

Immediate actions we completed (already in place):
- Disabled the autoscaling guard that incorrectly interpreted a transient runtime metric spike.
- Rolled forward a patch to the routing decision logic that avoids stale cache reads during autoscaler decisions.
- Increased observability thresholds and added an alert that fires earlier when queue depth rises for a tenant.

Committed next steps (owners and target dates):
- (Irene) Add cross-tenant canary checks to validate scaling decisions — target 2029-08-05.
- (Hannah) Formalize a runbook for queue-depth escalations and automated fallback routing — target 2029-08-02.
- (Logan) Provide a signed verification package with logs and sanitized traces for your security audit — target 2029-08-01.

We're making these changes with priority and will provide verification once each item is complete. Please find the attachments and links below; if you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute readout to walk through the timeline and answer any technical questions.

Attachments: quantumpay-rca-appendix.pdf (PDF), quantumpay-timeline.csv (CSV), post-incident-action-register.xlsx (XLSX)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1QPay-Quantumpay-RCA

Thanks —
Logan
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--

From: Samir Gupta <samir@quantumpay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@quantumpay.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jul 2029 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quantumpay service disruption: closure brief & remediation commitments

Logan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we book a readout: 

1) Can you confirm whether any customer-specific config was changed as part of the fix? We need assurance that configuration drift did not occur.
2) We'd like a sanitized extract of the request IDs (or session IDs) for our impacted runs so our internal tracing can cross-reference — is that possible?
3) Regarding the automation fallback, can you clarify whether that will route to a different model variant, a different region, or a degraded quality mode?

If you can address these in the readout or here in email, that will help our security and SRE teams. Thanks,

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
QuantumPay

On Sat, Jul 27, 2029 at 09:15 AM Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samir —
> 
> Thanks again for your patience while we completed the investigation. Attached is a concise closure brief that summarizes the root cause...

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jul 2029 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantumpay service disruption: closure brief & remediation commitments

Samir —

Answers inline below. Short version: no configuration drift observed; we can provide sanitized request/session IDs; fallback routing will be to a compatible model variant within the same region with soft-degraded quality, not cross-region. Details: 

1) Configuration changes: None were made to customer-specific configuration. The issue stemmed from an internal autoscaling heuristic that used a clustered runtime metric. The patch only updates the heuristic and the autoscaler behavior; we did not modify tenant configs or feature flags for QuantumPay. (Irene owns the verification artifacts.)

2) Request/session IDs: We can provide a sanitized list of impacted request IDs and the mapping to your internal session markers. We will remove full payloads and any PII; logs will be redacted following the standard shared policy. Expected delivery: 2029-08-01 (Logan).

3) Fallback behavior: The automated fallback will route to a model variant with the same architecture but a smaller token budget (quantization and a narrow attention window) within the same us-west region. That mode preserves semantic fidelity for most calls but may perform slightly differently on fringe edge cases. We will add an explicit opt-out switch per route, and document the behavior in the runbook.

Next steps:
- Schedule 30-minute readout (available windows: Mon 2029-07-29 10:00-12:00 PT or Tue 2029-07-30 14:00-16:00 PT).
- Deliver sanitized request IDs and verification package by 2029-08-01.
- Provide follow-up confirmation once the canary checks are in place (target 2029-08-05).

I'll open a JIRA for the verification artifacts so you can track progress: SUP-4821.

Thanks —
Logan

--

From: Samir Gupta <samir@quantumpay.com>

Subject: Re: Quantumpay service disruption: closure brief & remediation commitments

Logan / team —

Thanks for the clarity and for creating the verification artifacts. We confirm we will take the 30-minute readout on Mon 2029-07-29 at 10:30 PT. Agenda request: please include a short demo of the new alerting behavior and a walk-through of the sanitized log extraction process.

Also request for your compliance pack: once the verification is complete, please upload the signed verification package to the Drive link and post the HubSpot case update with the SUP-4821 reference so our procurement team can proceed with the closure and any credits.

Appreciate the responsiveness —
Samir
